There was no medical literature to support the position that warm working conditions could contribute to pneumonia or other respiratory tract infections.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.
Access to the worker's file was granted to the employer.

DecKeywords: Consequences of injury (residual weakness); Subsequent incidents (outside work)
DecSummary: The worker had been receiving temporary benefits for tendonitis of the right wrist since June 1981.  In December 1981, the worker fell down stairs at home, fracturing her right wrist and elbow.  The worker claimed that she was trying to turn on the light switch, which was located on the left wall, with her right hand when she slipped and that she attempted to grab the railing with her right hand but could not hang on due to weakness.  The Hearings Officer denied entitlement for the injuries resulting from the home accident.

DecKeywords: Board Directives and Guidelines (psychotraumatic disability) (five year guideline); Depression; Disability (disabled from working); Psychotraumatic disability
DecSummary: A truck driver appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer denying entitlement for psychotraumatic disability.  The worker suffered a back injury when he slipped and fell in 1968.  He was awarded a 5% pension in 1969, increased to 15% in 1974, to 20% in May 1983 and to 25% in October 1983.  He returned to his job in 1969 but had to give up trucking in 1979 due to increasing pain.  He then worked as a ship's carpenter at greatly reduced wages.  In 1983, the worker became depressed and attempted suicide.

DecKeywords: In the course of employment (travelling); Right to sue
DecSummary: The plaintiffs were involved in a motor vehicle accident.  One plaintiff was a door-to-door salesman of stereo equipment.  The other was an apprentice salesman who went along for training.  The accident occurred as they were driving to their first prospective customer.  It would have been impossible for them to make sales without use of a vehicle to transport them and their equipment.  The plaintiff's were in the course of employment.  Their right of action was taken away.

A bush worker was struck on the side of the head by portion of a tree.  He did not lose any time from work.  The worker was not entitled to further benefits.  The worker's neck condition was not related to the minor, temporary injury suffered in the accident but, rather, to preexisting degenerative disc disease.

The worker was receiving a pension of $127 per month, valued at about $14,500.  He had previously received a partial commutation in order to purchase a house.  He requested commutation of the remainder in order to renovate the house.  The Hearings Officer denied the commutation.  Since then, the worker sold the house and there were no monies remaining.  He now requested the commutation in order to purchase a car and trailer.  He had not worked in a considerable amount of years and would have no source of income if the request was granted.  The commutation was denied.

A sewing machine operator suffered a low back strain in September 1984.  The Board originally terminated benefits in July 1986 but the Hearings Officer granted 50% benefits.  The worker appealed the decision denying total temporary benefits.

DecKeywords: In the course of employment (takes self out of employment) (intoxication); Intoxication; Right to sue
DecSummary: The defendant was involved in a motor vehicle accident with the plaintiff.  The defendant was convicted of impaired driving and failing to give a breath sample.  The defendant had four or five beers at lunch.  He returned to work for the afternoon.  He left the plant before 4 o'clock.  The accident occurred at about 4:20.

DecKeywords: Automotive industry (assembler) (scuff job); Suitable employment; Epicondylitis
DecSummary: The worker sustained an injury in April 1980 which was diagnosed as right lateral epicondylitis.  He returned to modified work in April 1983 and performed a light job until November 23, 1983 when the job was terminated.

DecKeywords: Access to worker file, statutory (deletion of material); Access to worker file, statutory (issue in dispute) (particulars)
DecSummary: The worker objected to the release of medical records to the employer.  The worker sustained a low back injury in January 1987, underwent a discotomy in June 1987 and was considered able to return to work in November 1987.  It appeared that additional benefits were paid for periods of lay-off in December 1987 and January and February 1988.  It also appeared that there was a further lay-off in March and April of 1988.  In February 1989 the worker was awarded an 18% pension.

The worker hit her right elbow in December 1983.  She received benefits up until December 1984 for her resulting shoulder and arm sprain.  There was no medical evidence to support the worker's claim that she was disabled by reason of an organic condition beyond that date.

The worker appealed denial of a temporary supplement from December 1982 to October 1983.  The Board arranged a job for the worker.  The Board wanted the worker to work full time but the worker claimed she could only work part time.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (evidence to support Appeal Board conclusion)
DecSummary: The worker suffered a knee injury in 1971 and received temporary benefits until 1975.  The Appeal Board denied a pension for the knee disability and denied entitlement for a back disability that the worker claimed was related to the 1971 accident.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (evidence to support Appeal Board conclusion)
DecSummary: The Appeal Board denied benefits from 1978 and 1979, finding that the back disability was not related to a minor accident in 1965.  There was evidence to support the Appeal Board conclusion.  The Appeal Board preferred one medical opinion over another.  There was no error in law or fact which would give rise to doubt the correctness of the decision.
The worker appealed denial of benefits for a low back disability he claimed was related to an unwitnessed accident in February 1986.
The employer was appealing a decision entitling the worker to benefits for a low back disability which was found to be due to a disablement arising out of and in the course of employment.

DecKeywords: Adjournment (addition of representative); Chronic pain; Issue setting; Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board)
DecSummary: The worker appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer in July 1988 granting entitlement to 50% benefits from December 1981 until his pension assessment in March 1986 and confirming the pension at 10%.  In March 1989 the worker's file was returned to the WCB by Tribunal counsel pursuant to Practice Direction No. 9.  The Board advised the worker that chronic pain benefits were denied and the worker appealed at the Board.
The worker was exposed to noise from 1959 to 1979.  Entitlement was denied by the Board on the basis that hearing loss did not reach compensable levels until 1973.

The worker suffered from sensorineural hearing loss of 45 decibels in one ear and 40 decibels in the other.  The worker was a cupola (furnace) operator in a foundry from 1966 to 1974.  At the very least, the worker was exposed to noise at the 85 decibel level for a five year period, with times when the exposure level was greater.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (consideration of evidence)
DecSummary: The Appeal Board denied temporary benefits subsequent to 1977 and denied any benefits after expiry of a two year pension for psychotraumatic disability in 1979.
The worker fell in February 1985.  He appealed a decision of the Hearings Officer terminating benefits in July 1988.

DecKeywords: Leave to appeal (good reason to doubt correctness) (evidence to support Appeal Board conclusion)
DecSummary: There was evidence to support the Appeal Board conclusion that the worker's degenerative disc disease was not related to compensable back injuries suffered in 1971 or 1975 and that the worker did not injure his back in an accident in 1980.  The issue of whether the condition was related to the nature of work prior to 1969 was never before the Board at any level.  In any event, there was nothing in the medical evidence to establish such a claim.
The worker was receiving a 10% pension, valued at about $46,000.  The worker wanted a partial commutation in order to discharge the second mortgage on his home.

DecKeywords: Rheumatoid arthritis; Dependency benefits (death results from an injury); Silicosis; Mining; Pneumonia (interstitial)
DecSummary: The worker's wife appealed a decision of the Appeals Adjudicator denying dependency benefits.  The worker was a miner from 1955 to 1979.  In January 1980, he developed joint pain and swelling, diagnosed as rheumatoid arthritis.  In April 1980, he died from fulminating diffuse interstitial pneumonia.  In addition, the autopsy indicated the presence of anthrasilicotic nodules in the worker's lungs.

DecKeywords: Hearing loss; Medical opinion (hearing loss) (testing procedures)
DecSummary: The Hearings Officer had found that the worker's hearing loss was due to a combination of middle ear disease and noise exposure.  The noise exposure loss was found to be sufficient to warrant a claim for medical benefits, but not a claim for a pension.  The worker appealed, claiming entitlement to a pension.

The Panel found that the worker did in fact suffer an injury by accident while pushing a bin which resulted in a left chest disability.  The employer argued that there was insufficient evidence of an accident and pointed to the worker's prior concerns regarding heart problems as well as his heavy smoking.  The medical evidence ruled out the issue of cardiac problems and established that the worker was suffering from strained chest muscles in the left chest wall.  There was evidence of immediate onset of pain, immediate complaint, lay-off and treatment.

The worker claimed entitlement for a back condition, diagnosed as ankylosing spondylitis.  The worker had preexisting ankylosing spondylitis.  This condition can become symptomatic on its own or as a result of trauma.  The worker claimed that the onset of pain occurred after lifting a patient.  However, people to whom the worker allegedly reported the accident could not be found or could not remember.  The worker did not see a doctor until 12 days after the alleged accident and did not report the accident for more than two weeks after that.

DecKeywords: Jurisdiction, Tribunal (final decision of Board); Reconsideration (jurisdiction)
DecSummary: The worker's widow applied to reconsider Decision No. 266/89, in which the hearing panel denied the worker entitlement for leukemia which he claimed was related to workplace exposure to pesticides on one specific day when a container broke open.

DecKeywords: Reconsideration (consideration of evidence); Procedure (records retention schedules)
DecSummary: The worker's estate applied for reconsideration of Decision No. 63/89.
